meta.title: Frankenstein, Volumes 1 and 2 (1818 text, pp. 7-111)
meta.note: All content was written from memory of the novel and is NOT verified against the student's edition. Every item has verified=false until a person checks it.

passage-a.title: The creature to Victor on Montanvert
passage-a.text: "I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed. Everywhere I see bliss, from which I alone am irrevocably excluded. I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend. Make me happy, and I shall again be virtuous."

passage-b.title: Victor to Walton
passage-b.text: "Learn from me, if not by my precepts, at least by my example, how dangerous is the acquirement of knowledge, and how much happier that man is who believes his native town to be the world, than he who aspires to become greater than his nature will allow."

passage-c.title: Victor on the creature as his vampire
passage-c.text: "I considered the being whom I had cast among mankind, and endowed with the will and power to effect purposes of horror, such as the deed which he had now done, nearly in the light of my own vampire, my own spirit let loose from the grave, and forced to destroy all that was dear to me."

passage-d.title: The creature's first memories
passage-d.text: "It is with considerable difficulty that I remember the original aera of my being: all the events of that period appear confused and indistinct. A strange multiplicity of sensations seized me, and I saw, felt, heard, and smelt, at the same time; and it was, indeed, a long time before I learned to distinguish between the operations of my various senses."

questions.answer: His sister, Margaret Saville
distractors: Elizabeth Lavenza
His mother
Henry Clerval

questions.prompt: What is Walton's goal as he sails north?
questions.answer: To reach the North Pole and make a great discovery
distractors: To find Victor Frankenstein
To escape his debts
To hunt whales for profit

questions.prompt: At which university does Victor study natural philosophy and chemistry?
questions.answer: Ingolstadt
distractors: Geneva
Oxford
Paris

questions.prompt: Which professor encourages Victor's interest in chemistry and modern science?

Alphonse Frankenstein
Mr. Kirwin

The magistrate at Justine's trial

distractors: Victor's cousin and fiancee
Elizabeth's older sister
Safie's maid

She hopes Victor will pardon her

He is angry at Justine

questions.prompt: Who says: "Do your duty towards me, and I will do mine towards you and the rest of mankind"?
questions.answer: The creature, to Victor
distractors: Victor, to Walton
Alphonse, to Victor
Felix, to Safie

distractors: Agatha's friend who hides the creature
The blind man's wife
A servant of the Frankensteins

questions.prompt: How does the creature secretly help the De Laceys?
questions.answer: He gathers firewood and clears snow for them
distractors: He leaves food at their door
He repairs their roof
He sends them money

questions.prompt: Which member of the De Lacey family does NOT flee in fear when first meeting the creature?
questions.answer: The blind old man, De Lacey
distractors: Felix
Agatha
Safie

questions.prompt: Which book leads the creature to compare himself to both Adam and Satan?
questions.answer: Paradise Lost
distractors: Plutarch's Lives
The Sorrows of Werter
Ruins of Empires

questions.prompt: What does the creature demand that Victor make for him?
questions.answer: A female companion
distractors: A home in Geneva
A cure for his appearance
A new body

questions.prompt: Which writers fascinate Victor as a boy, only to be dismissed by his father?
questions.answer: Cornelius Agrippa, Paracelsus, and Albertus Magnus
distractors: Newton, Galileo, and Bacon
Milton, Plutarch, and Goethe
Locke, Voltaire, and Rousseau

questions.prompt: Why does Victor flee from his laboratory right after the creature comes to life?
questions.answer: The creature's appearance fills him with horror and disgust, shattering his dream
distractors: He fears the creature will attack him
He runs to get Clerval's help
He believes his experiment failed to create life

questions.prompt: After Justine's execution, Victor travels to Chamounix and the Alps. What does this setting do in the story?
questions.answer: Nature's grandeur gives him brief relief from his guilt
distractors: It reminds him of Elizabeth
It is where he plans to build a second creature
It is a place to hide from the creature

questions.prompt: The creature decides to stop stealing food from the cottagers. What does this show about him?
questions.answer: He feels sympathy and realizes his actions make them suffer
distractors: He is afraid of being caught
He no longer needs to eat
He wants to starve himself

questions.prompt: Why does the creature wait until only old De Lacey is home to introduce himself?
questions.answer: The old man is blind and cannot judge him by his appearance
distractors: The old man is the weakest and easiest to overpower
He wants to steal something from the cottage
He believes De Lacey knows Victor

questions.prompt: What is the effect of the creature seeing his own reflection in a pool?
questions.answer: He understands why humans fear him and feels ashamed
distractors: He feels proud of his strength
He decides to disguise himself
He decides to return to Victor

questions.prompt: Why does the creature see himself in both Adam and Satan?
questions.answer: Like Adam he was made by a creator, but he is abandoned and feels envy like Satan
distractors: Both were punished for stealing fire
Both were raised by a loving family
Both were rescued by their creators

questions.prompt: Why does the creature kill William and frame Justine?
questions.answer: To take revenge on Victor and his family, driven by rage at being rejected
distractors: William attacked him first
He was trying to rescue William
Justine had harmed him earlier

questions.prompt: Why does Shelley frame Victor's story with Walton's letters?
questions.answer: Walton's ambition mirrors Victor's, and Victor's story warns of its cost
distractors: To prove the creature is real
To show Walton is a better scientist than Victor
To explain how the creature learned language

questions.prompt: Who is speaking, and to whom?
questions.answer: The creature, to Victor
distractors: Victor, to Walton
The creature, to old De Lacey
Victor, to Clerval

questions.prompt: What is the creature arguing by comparing himself to Adam and the fallen angel?
questions.answer: Victor, as his creator, has failed in his duty and made him miserable
distractors: He deserves to be punished like Satan
He wants to be worshipped as a god
He hopes to be forgiven by God

questions.prompt: What does "misery made me a fiend" suggest?
questions.answer: His cruelty comes from how he has been treated, not from his nature
distractors: He was born evil
He enjoys being a fiend
He was never good

questions.prompt: In this passage, "irrevocably" most nearly means:
questions.answer: In a way that cannot be undone
distractors: Temporarily
Willingly
Secretly

questions.prompt: Who is speaking, and to whom?
questions.answer: Victor, to Walton
distractors: The creature, to Victor
Alphonse, to Victor
Victor, to Elizabeth

questions.prompt: What is the main warning in this passage?
questions.answer: Ambition that goes beyond human limits leads to ruin
distractors: Knowledge should never be taught in schools
Travel is more dangerous than study
Only the old should seek knowledge

questions.prompt: What does "believes his native town to be the world" suggest?
questions.answer: Contentment with a small, ordinary life can bring more happiness
distractors: Everyone should live in Geneva
Education is a waste of time
The world is smaller than people think

questions.prompt: Why is it fitting that Victor says this to this listener?
questions.answer: Walton shares Victor's ambition and is risking his own life for glory
distractors: Walton has given up exploring
Walton is Victor's close relative
Walton has just met the creature

questions.prompt: What do Walton's crew see on the ice shortly before they find Victor?
questions.answer: A sledge drawn by dogs and driven by a figure of gigantic size
distractors: A second expedition ship sending signals of distress
A lone traveler waving a flag from a floating iceberg
A frozen ship with its crew missing from the deck

questions.prompt: What event first makes fifteen-year-old Victor doubt the old alchemists and turn toward modern science?
questions.answer: Lightning destroys an oak tree near his family's country home
distractors: A fire destroys the library of his father's house
Elizabeth falls gravely ill with a sudden fever
A visiting professor mocks the books he is reading

questions.prompt: How does Caroline Frankenstein die?
questions.answer: Of scarlet fever, caught while nursing Elizabeth
distractors: Of a fever, caught while nursing Justine
Of grief, after the loss of her youngest son
Of an injury, after a carriage accident near Geneva

questions.prompt: Which dream torments Victor right after the creature first opens its eyes?
questions.answer: Elizabeth turns into the corpse of his dead mother in his arms
distractors: The creature strangles William before his eyes
Justine is led to the scaffold while he watches
He is lost on a frozen sea with no way home

questions.prompt: How does M. Krempe react when Victor says he has read Agrippa and Paracelsus?
questions.answer: He says Victor has wasted his time and must start his studies over
distractors: He praises Victor's curiosity and invites him to join his lab
He reports Victor to the university for studying forbidden books
He lends Victor his own books on alchemy to continue reading

questions.prompt: How does Victor learn that William has been murdered?
questions.answer: A letter from his father
distractors: A visit from Henry Clerval at Ingolstadt
A letter from Elizabeth, written from Belrive
A report from a magistrate in Geneva

questions.prompt: Where does Victor first come to suspect the creature killed William?
questions.answer: Near Geneva at night, when a flash of lightning reveals a gigantic figure
distractors: At the scene of the murder, when he sees the body
In a dream, on the night before his return to Geneva
At Justine's trial, when she names the creature

questions.prompt: Who says: "Alas! Victor, when falsehood can look so like the truth, who can assure themselves of certain happiness?"
questions.answer: Elizabeth
distractors: Justine
Clerval
Victor's father

questions.prompt: In his story, the creature repeats the words of a boy who says his father is a syndic named Frankenstein. Who is the boy, and why does this matter?
questions.answer: William; it tells the creature the boy is part of Victor's family
distractors: Felix; it tells the creature the cottagers know Victor
Ernest; it tells the creature Victor lives in the mountains
William; it tells the creature the boy is Justine's brother

questions.prompt: What does the creature do with William's locket?
questions.answer: Plants it in the folds of Justine's dress while she sleeps
distractors: Throws it into a lake to hide the crime
Returns it to Victor as proof of his power
Hides it in the hovel beside the De Laceys' cottage

questions.prompt: How does the creature react the first time he discovers fire?
questions.answer: He feels delight at its warmth, then pain after touching the flame
distractors: He feels fear and flees deeper into the forest
He feels indifference until the cold drives him back
He feels anger and tries to stamp it out

questions.prompt: Where does the creature find the books that shape his view of the world?
questions.answer: In a leather portmanteau left in a wood
distractors: In Victor's laboratory, in the pockets of his coat
In the De Laceys' cottage, while the family is away
In a village library, after dark

questions.prompt: How does the creature learn the details of his own creation?
questions.answer: He reads a journal in the pocket of the coat he took from Victor's lab
distractors: Safie explains it to him as part of her lessons
Old De Lacey tells him after hearing his story
He finds Victor's letters in Felix's possession

questions.prompt: Why is Safie's father imprisoned in Paris?
questions.answer: He is a Turkish merchant condemned partly because of his religion and wealth
distractors: He is a French noble arrested for unpaid debts
He is an Arab sailor accused of piracy at sea
He is a Genevese magistrate accused of fraud

questions.prompt: In his speech on Montanvert, what does the creature say he is, in contrast to Adam?
questions.answer: The fallen angel
distractors: The wandering exile
The prodigal son
The sleeping giant

questions.prompt: Elizabeth says she feels as if she is walking on the edge of a precipice. What does this suggest?
questions.answer: Justine's fate shows that innocence is no protection, so no one feels safe
distractors: She suspects that Victor is hiding something from her
She wants to leave Geneva and return to Italy
She is afraid of the mountains near the lake

questions.prompt: Why does Shelley let the creature tell his own story?
questions.answer: To make readers see him as a thinking, feeling being instead of a simple monster
distractors: To prove that Victor's account is completely false
To show that the creature is stronger than Victor
To lighten the mood after Justine's trial

questions.prompt: Why does the creature stop stealing food from the cottagers?
questions.answer: He realizes his thefts deepen their poverty and he feels pity for them
distractors: He fears that Felix will catch him in the act
He finds enough berries and roots in the forest
Old De Lacey asks him to stop

questions.prompt: Lightning appears again and again around Victor (the oak, the storm over Geneva). What does it suggest?
questions.answer: Knowledge and power can be destructive, which foreshadows the violence to come
distractors: Nature is on Victor's side and guides him
Victor is protected by his mother's memory
Storms mirror Elizabeth's fear of the mountains

questions.prompt: Why is it significant that old De Lacey is the only one who listens kindly to the creature?
questions.answer: He is blind, which shows that prejudice rests on appearance
distractors: He is the oldest, and so the wisest of the family
He is the only one who has ever met Victor
He is the only one who speaks the creature's language

questions.prompt: What does the creature's reaction to Paradise Lost reveal?
questions.answer: He sees himself as an abandoned creation who feels envy like Satan
distractors: He believes he is destined for heaven
He decides that books are not to be trusted
He decides to become a teacher to humankind

questions.prompt: What is the effect of the creature burning the De Lacey cottage?
questions.answer: It marks his shift from hoping for acceptance to vowing revenge on humanity
distractors: It shows he wants to hide his tracks from Victor

questions.prompt: Why is the subtitle "The Modern Prometheus" fitting for Victor?

distractors: Like Prometheus, he is rescued from his punishment by a god

questions.prompt: What does "my own vampire" suggest about Victor's view of the creature?
questions.answer: The creature is a destructive force tied to Victor himself and fed by his guilt
distractors: The creature drinks blood and must be hunted
The creature is the ghost of Victor's mother
The creature is a danger only to strangers

questions.prompt: What does "cast among mankind" imply about Victor's actions?
questions.answer: Victor is responsible for releasing a danger into the world
distractors: He carefully introduced the creature to society
He banished the creature from Geneva by law
He hoped mankind would welcome the creature

questions.prompt: Which "deed" is Victor referring to?
questions.answer: The murder of William
distractors: The execution of Justine
The death of his mother
The creature's attack on Felix

questions.prompt: Which phrase best describes Victor's tone in this passage?
questions.answer: Dread mixed with guilt
distractors: Calm pride
Hopeful determination
Cheerful curiosity

questions.prompt: What does "a strange multiplicity of sensations" convey?
questions.answer: The creature is overwhelmed because he cannot yet tell his senses apart
distractors: The creature is in great physical pain
The creature is enjoying a feeling of power
The creature is confused by Victor's words

questions.prompt: In this passage, "original aera of my being" most nearly means:
questions.answer: The very beginning of his existence
distractors: His earliest memory of Victor's face
The place where he was created
His first friendship with a human

questions.prompt: Why does Shelley begin the creature's story with this confusion?
questions.answer: To show him as newborn and innocent, shaped by experience rather than born evil
distractors: To suggest he has a damaged mind
To hint that he has supernatural powers
To prove that Victor's science failed

questions.prompt: Which later event most closely echoes this passage's theme of learning through the senses?
questions.answer: He burns his hand reaching toward a fire
distractors: He reads Paradise Lost in the forest
Safie arrives at the cottage
He meets William near Geneva

characters.name: Victor Frankenstein
characters.role: Narrator of the main story and creator of the creature
characters.notes: Ambitious, then guilty and secretive. Abandons his creation and stays silent about it. Compared to Prometheus.

characters.name: The creature
characters.role: Victor's creation, who is never given a name
characters.notes: Starts out innocent and kind. Rejection turns him bitter. Educated by watching the De Laceys and by reading.

characters.name: Robert Walton
characters.role: Arctic explorer who frames the story
characters.notes: His ambition mirrors Victor's. He writes to his sister, Margaret Saville.

characters.name: Alphonse Frankenstein
characters.notes: Dismisses Agrippa without explaining. Writes the letter about William.

characters.name: Caroline Beaufort
characters.notes: Takes in Elizabeth and Justine. Dies of scarlet fever caught from Elizabeth.

characters.name: Elizabeth Lavenza
characters.notes: Writes to Victor. Defends Justine and is shaken by her death.

characters.name: William
characters.notes: Killed by the creature, who takes his locket.

characters.name: Justine Moritz
characters.role: Servant raised in the Frankenstein household
characters.notes: Falsely accused of William's murder and executed. Confesses under pressure from her confessor.

characters.name: M. Waldman
characters.notes: Encourages Victor's interest in chemistry and modern science.

characters.name: Old De Lacey
characters.notes: The only one who listens kindly to the creature, because he cannot see him.

characters.name: Felix and Agatha
characters.notes: Felix beats the creature. Agatha faints.

characters.name: Safie
characters.role: Turkish merchant's daughter who loves Felix
characters.notes: Her arrival lets the creature learn language and the family's history.

vocab.definition: Passionate and intense; showing strong enthusiasm or devotion
To give in or surrender, often after resisting
A mythical creature made of parts of different animals; also a wild or impossible fantasy
Harshness of weather; stormy or severe conditions
Inspiring awe through vast, powerful beauty, often mixed with fear
